summary.architecture: Single-process Flask application with route handlers, cryptographic/JWT helpers, parser/evaluation helpers and database bootstrap in main.py.
summary.normal_deployment: Direct execution of main.py starts Flask on configured address and port, defaulting to 127.0.0.1:4000 with SQLite :memory: unless database CLI options select an external backend.
primary_data_flows: HTTP form/query/cookie input to Flask route handlers
Route handlers to OS command execution, Python eval, pickle deserialization, XML parser, Jinja template renderer, AES decryptor, JWT verifier and database cursor
Startup CLI/environment inputs to key initialization and database bootstrap

assets.name: Python process authority
assets.description: Application memory, route globals, database cursor, crypto/JWT keys and host permissions of the Flask process.

assets.name: JWT signing and verification keys
assets.description: SIGN_KEY creates tokens; VERIFY_KEY verifies tokens and is used to emit JWK material.

assets.name: Authentication cookie and admin authorization state
assets.description: authentication cookie controls /user; sub == admin controls admin response state.

assets.name: CONFIG hidden entries
assets.description: CONFIG contains base64-encoded references to KEY and ADMIN_SECRET plus public app metadata.

assets.name: Relational database contents
assets.description: public_stuff and secret_stuff tables are created and seeded; public_stuff is queried by /listservices.

assets.name: Local filesystem and network-reachable resources
assets.description: Resources reachable by process permissions, XML parser behavior or OS command execution.

starting_capabilities: Send GET and POST requests to reachable routes
Set query parameters, form fields and cookies
absent_privileges: Does not initially control Flask process
Does not initially control database server
Does not initially possess signing key or admin authorization

starting_capabilities: Can obtain a normal guest JWT using guest:guest
absent_privileges: Does not initially have admin subject claim

starting_capabilities: Can reach app if operator binds it beyond default loopback

security_objectives.objective: Untrusted HTTP inputs should not gain process, OS, parser, template, database or cryptographic authority beyond the intended workflow.
JWT verification should preserve claim integrity before /user accepts sub == admin as admin state.
Database query input should not cross from filter data into database command structure.
Hidden configuration values and key material should not be disclosed through config selector processing or downstream process authority.

threats.title: Python evaluation grants process-level authority
threats.threat_scenario: An unauthenticated client submits expression content that is evaluated by the server-side Python interpreter.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated web client able to reach /evaluate.
threats.affected_asset: Flask process authority, in-memory secrets, database cursor, filesystem/network permissions available to the process.
trust_boundaries_crossed: External HTTP client to Flask route
Flask route to Python interpreter execution context
attack_path: Client sends POST form field expression
preconditions: Attacker can send POST requests to the app
/evaluate route is reachable
Expression evaluation has access to Python runtime context
threats.potential_impact: Process-level code execution or inspection of in-memory state and accessible resources, depending on runtime permissions.
existing_controls: Expression is processed only when POST body supplies it
security_gaps: No boundary between user input and interpreter evaluation
Interpreter context shares process authority with keys, config and database cursor

threats.title: DNS lookup crosses into OS command execution
threats.threat_scenario: An unauthenticated client controls part of a command string executed through the operating system command interface.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated web client able to reach /lookup.
threats.affected_asset: OS process boundary, Flask process host environment, filesystem/network resources available to the process.
trust_boundaries_crossed: External HTTP client to Flask route
Flask route to OS command/process boundary
attack_path: Client submits POST form field address
Route builds nslookup command by concatenating address
preconditions: Attacker can send POST requests
App host has a shell/command environment compatible with popen
Command execution inherits process permissions
threats.potential_impact: Execution of unintended OS-level commands or access to host resources reachable by the app process.
existing_controls: Command string is prefixed with nslookup
security_gaps: HTTP input is concatenated into a shell command
No authentication or argument boundary before popen
assumptions_or_unknowns: Shell parsing behavior and available commands depend on OS and deployment
README default binds to loopback unless configured otherwise

threats.title: Cookie deserialization transfers client state into Python object loading
threats.threat_scenario: A client-controlled cookie is decoded and passed to Python deserialization during a GET request.
threats.threat_actor: Web client able to set its own value cookie and request /cookie.
threats.affected_component: cookie() route and Python pickle deserializer
threats.affected_asset: Python process authority and application memory.
trust_boundaries_crossed: Client-controlled cookie store to Flask request
Request cookie bytes to Python deserialization
attack_path: Resulting object is converted to string and rendered
preconditions: Attacker can control the value cookie
Route receives a GET request with the cookie present
Pickle payload is accepted by the runtime
threats.potential_impact: Process-level effects during deserialization or unexpected object creation, depending on payload and runtime environment.
existing_controls: POST-created cookie values are generated with pickle.dumps and base64
security_gaps: No server-side signing or verification of cookie provenance
Client-held cookie contents are trusted as serialized Python data
assumptions_or_unknowns: Custom HTTP clients can set cookie contents
Runtime impact depends on available Python modules and process permissions

threats.title: Server-side template rendering evaluates constructed user-influenced template source
threats.threat_scenario: A client-controlled name is interpolated into a template string before Jinja rendering.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated web client able to submit /sayhi.
threats.affected_asset: Template execution context, Flask process state and reachable runtime objects.
trust_boundaries_crossed: External HTTP form input to Flask route
Constructed server-side string to Jinja template engine
attack_path: Route formats name into greeting HTML
Route formats greeting into template string
preconditions: Attacker can submit POST requests
Jinja evaluates template syntax present in constructed template
threats.potential_impact: Server-side template expression evaluation and access to template/runtime context, depending on available objects.
existing_controls: No explicit route control observed before rendering
security_gaps: User input becomes part of template source
No explicit escaping or sandbox boundary before rendering
assumptions_or_unknowns: Accessible template globals depend on Flask/Jinja runtime version and context

threats.title: SQL query construction crosses from public filter input into database authority
threats.threat_scenario: A client-controlled category filter is interpolated into SQL executed through the application database cursor.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated web client able to request /listservices with a category parameter.
threats.affected_component: listservices() route, global DB cursor and selected database backend.
threats.affected_asset: public_stuff, secret_stuff, database metadata and database connection authority.
trust_boundaries_crossed: External query parameter to Flask route
Route string construction to SQL parser/database engine
preconditions: Attacker can reach /listservices
Database setup completed and global cursor exists
Backend SQL dialect accepts the resulting query shape
threats.potential_impact: Unauthorized database reads or manipulation of query semantics, including potential access to seeded secret_stuff, depending on backend behavior and DB privileges.
existing_controls: Route starts with SELECT * from public_stuff
Execution exceptions are caught and returned as response text
security_gaps: User input is embedded into SQL text rather than bound as data
Route uses same database connection authority established at startup
assumptions_or_unknowns: Multi-statement support and SQL grammar vary by backend
Database user privileges depend on CLI-supplied credentials and external DB configuration

threats.title: JWT algorithm trust boundary can permit admin-state bypass
threats.threat_scenario: A client-held JWT controls /user authorization while verification dispatch trusts the token header algorithm across RS256, HS256 and None paths.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated client or authenticated guest able to submit an authentication cookie.
threats.affected_component: JWT creation/verification helpers and jwtmain() admin check.
threats.affected_asset: Admin authorization state and integrity of authentication claims.
trust_boundaries_crossed: Unverified JWT header to verification algorithm dispatch
attack_path: Client places token in authentication cookie
verify_token uses jwt.get_unverified_header and dispatches by alg
/user grants admin response when sub == admin
preconditions: Attacker can set the authentication cookie
Target accepts one enabled algorithm path
Claims satisfy issuer, audience and time checks in chosen verifier
threats.potential_impact: Unauthorized transition from guest or unauthenticated state to the app's admin response state.
existing_controls: RS256 verification uses PyJWT audience and issuer checks
Manual HS256/None paths check audience, issuer, time and signature or empty signature conditions
security_gaps: Algorithm choice comes from untrusted token headers
Authorization relies only on token subject after verification dispatch
assumptions_or_unknowns: Exact exploitability depends on PyJWT behavior, token construction and runtime clock
No broader admin backend exists beyond the response state in this repository

threats.title: Config selector decryption exposes cryptographic oracle toward hidden config values
threats.threat_scenario: Client-controlled key bytes are decrypted by the server and decryption/padding errors are returned.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated web client able to request /config.
threats.affected_component: AES-CBC decrypt/unpad helpers and config() route.
threats.affected_asset: CONFIG hidden entries, including KEY and ADMIN_SECRET references; crypto key material in process memory.
trust_boundaries_crossed: External query parameter to hex decoder
attack_path: Route creates encrypted links for viewable app_ keys
Route calls unhexlify and decrypt(kv, KEY)
Exceptions are returned as response text
If decrypted text names any CONFIG key, route displays that value
preconditions: Attacker can query /config
Attacker can observe response differences or errors
Runtime KEY remains stable for process lifetime
threats.potential_impact: Disclosure of hidden config values or oracle-assisted inference about encrypted selector validity, depending on cryptographic interaction and request volume.
existing_controls: Page only links keys starting with app_
Unknown decrypted keys are not displayed unless they match CONFIG.keys()
security_gaps: Decrypt/unpad operation is exposed to unauthenticated callers
Successful decrypted selectors are checked against all CONFIG keys rather than only viewable keys
assumptions_or_unknowns: Practical disclosure depends on request observability and oracle properties
No rate limiting or monitoring code was found

threats.title: XML parser boundary can reach local or network resources
threats.threat_scenario: Untrusted XML is parsed with DTD loading and network-enabled parser options.
threats.threat_actor: Unauthenticated web client able to submit XML to /xml.
threats.affected_asset: Local files and network destinations reachable by XML parser/runtime; response confidentiality of parsed/serialized XML output.
trust_boundaries_crossed: External HTTP form input to Flask route
XML bytes to parser entity/DTD processing
attack_path: Route constructs etree.XMLParser with no_network=False and load_dtd=True
Serialized result is escaped and returned
preconditions: Attacker can send POST XML
Parser/runtime supports relevant external resource resolution
Target resources are reachable by process permissions or network
threats.potential_impact: Disclosure or interaction with local/network resources through XML parsing behavior, plus resource-consumption risk from large or complex XML.
existing_controls: Serialized XML is passed through html.escape before response rendering
No active try/except around parser execution
security_gaps: Parser is configured to load DTDs with network access
Route has no authentication or resource policy
assumptions_or_unknowns: Actual file/network access depends on libxml2/lxml behavior, deployment network policy and process filesystem permissions

threat_relationships.description: These paths all move unauthenticated HTTP-controlled data toward process or execution authority and can expose overlapping downstream assets.
T5 targets the DB directly through SQL construction; process-authority paths may reach database state indirectly through globals and modules.
JWT bypass depends on token verification trust; key/config exposure or process authority can undermine the same authorization boundary through separate paths.

threat_relationships.relationship: Local and network resource access linkage
threat_relationships.description: OS command execution and XML parser resource resolution can both cross from HTTP input toward host or network resources through different components.

assumptions_unknowns_architectural_weakn.item: Default listen address is loopback, but CLI can bind elsewhere.
No centralized authentication middleware protects sensitive routes; only /user performs token-based authorization.
Sensitive consumers are embedded directly in route handlers in a single process.
No SECURITY.md policy, automated tests, CI policy, deployment manifest or production WSGI config was found in the repository intelligence pass.
The application is intentionally vulnerable by stated project purpose; this model treats boundaries as threat scenarios, not remediation instructions.
